subject: Next steps: on-prem egress acceptance & PII retention checklist
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Hassan <amira.hassan@novafin.com>, infra@novafin.com
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps: on-prem egress acceptance & PII retention checklist

Hi Amira / NovaFin infra team —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth:

1) Primary constraints you reiterated
   - All customer PII and transaction payloads must remain inside the NovaFin VPC; no persistent copies may be stored in our hosted buckets.
   - Audit logs (transaction-level) required for 7 years; operational debug/logs retained 30 days.
   - No direct internet egress for model activations — outbound only via a customer-managed egress gateway you control.
   - Air-gapped option may be required for select environments; will need an on-prem package evaluation.

2) Action items (owner / ETA)
   - NovaFin: confirm whether the egress gateway supports outbound TLS inspection bypass for Redwood IPs (Amira / infra@novafin.com) — target: 3/23.
   - Redwood infra: propose minimal NAT/proxy rules + port allowlist and a service-account pattern for the connector (Rishi) — target: 3/24.
   - Legal/Procurement: review privacy annex uploaded by NovaFin (attachment: novafin-privacy-annex.pdf) and flag any OS/terms conflicts (Lauren) — target: 3/26.

3) Technical clarifications we need from NovaFin
   - Which subnets will host the connector? Will the connector be allowed outbound to our API endpoints or must it push to an on-prem queue only?
   - KMS/HSM requirement for keys used to encrypt any ephemeral cache — yes/no?
   - Are there any mandatory egress allowlists (IPs/FQDNs) or must we support an egress proxy with TLS passthrough?

Attachments included: postcall-network-sketch.png (diagram I drew during the call).

Proposed follow-up: 30-minute technical alignment with NovaFin infra + our infra (Rishi, Soojin) on 3/24 or 3/25. If 3/24 works we can finalize the connector spec and send a narrow SOC/PCI-exec checklist.

Thanks —

Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

From: Amira Hassan <amira.hassan@novafin.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra@novafin.com
Date: 2027-03-21T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: on-prem egress acceptance & PII retention checklist

Thanks Lauren — clear summary. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- Confirmed requirements:
  * Transaction-level records (payment/settlement) must be retained 7 years for regulatory audits.
  * Debug/diagnostic logs can be 30 days.
  * PII (names, SSNs, account numbers) cannot persist outside the VPC — no hosted S3 or external datastore.

- Egress gateway
  * Our infra operates an outbound egress proxy in the DMZ with an allowlist. We can add Redwood's egress endpoints but would prefer TLS passthrough to avoid TLS MITM.
  * The gateway supports an allowlist by IP and FQDN; we'll need Redwood to provide predictable endpoints/FQDNs.

- KMS
  * We require customer-managed keys (KMS) for any encrypted caches. HSM not required but could be later.

I attached our privacy annex (novafin-privacy-annex.pdf) for your legal review.

I'll coordinate with our infra team on availability — 3/24 midday should be fine.

Best,
Amira Hassan
Head of Platform Security, NovaFin
amira.hassan@novafin.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amira Hassan <amira.hassan@novafin.com>, infra@novafin.com
Date: 2027-03-21T14:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: on-prem egress acceptance & PII retention checklist

Looping in some implementation notes from infra to help the 3/24 alignment:

Top-level proposal
- Use a small connector VM (customer-managed) inside NovaFin private subnets. Connector initiates outbound TLS connections to Redwood over port 443 and authenticates with a short-lived mTLS cert. No inbound ports required.

Egress patterns
- TLS passthrough is preferred: we can recommend using SNI-based allowlisting for FQDNs plus a small IP range for redundancy. We need Amira's team to share the allowed FQDNs/IPs.
- If their gateway demands a proxy that terminates TLS, we will provide a cert bundle and handle TLS to the endpoint, but that will require KMS wrap for ephemeral cache keys.

Data handling
- Ephemeral KV cache will be local to the connector and encrypted with customer KMS; we will never write PII to disk longer than the TTL (default: 60s) unless explicitly requested.
- Audit logs: Redwood can stream operational logs back to NovaFin's syslog endpoint via an outbound syslog TLS session (port 6514) so logs never traverse public storage.

Questions for NovaFin (to confirm before 3/24 meeting)
1) Do you have a preferred PKI / CA for issuing connector certs?
2) Can the egress gateway allow outbound mTLS to our advertised FQDNs, or must we route to a proxy endpoint?
3) Will you accept a short-lived token exchange (OIDC) for API auth instead of long-lived API keys?

I attached a short proposal (rishi-egress-proposal.pdf) with a recommended connector manifest and firewall rule set. Happy to walk through during the call.

- Rishi
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
